summary: The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, but both the input gate and the scientific gate failed. Studio did not run: the simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false, and the stated reason is that a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object. The extraction supplies an empty floorplan and empty power_w because the paper publishes no block coordinates, sizes or per-block watts. The selected scenario is the ThermoDSE 'Ours' row of Table IV (5x4 NPU cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm spacing, 300 mm2 and 75 C limits). The paper reports a HotSpot 6.0 steady-state peak of 74.8 C under 45 C ambient and 0.4 K/W convection. This would have been a custom 2D steady run with no transient trace, and it did not execute. There is no Studio temperature, so no numerical comparison with 74.8 C is made, and comparison_valid is false. Independent verification, the adversarial code, parameter, config and data checks and the page/asset evidence review are all unresolved. The paper's 74.8 C figure is therefore a cited source value only, not a reproduced or validated result. Nothing here supports a claim of replication, even approximate. Qualitatively, the paper's design is thermally constrained near its 75 C limit, but that is the authors' own reported result, not something this pipeline confirmed.
limitations: Studio was skipped, so there is no simulated temperature and no basis for a numerical comparison with the 74.8 C peak.

The extraction has an empty floorplan and an empty power_w, so the custom 2D steady input is invalid. No block geometry or per-block watts are published, and total energy and delay were not split into block power.

Evidence items 0-24 lack valid page or asset locators, no cited thermal observable or steady/transient regime was accepted, and independent review and the adversarial code, parameter, config and data checks are unresolved.

The paper's model is 2.5D with chiplets and an I/O die on a passive interposer, plus a TIM, heat spreader and heat sink stack. A 2D steady Studio solve could at most be an illustrative screening of that, not a faithful HotSpot 6.0 replication.
Interposer, TIM, spreader and heat sink material properties and geometries are only referenced to TESA and HotSpot defaults, so boundary and material assumptions cannot be matched.

The reported 74.8 C is a peak from time-averaged power over a sequential multi-DNN workload. The hotspot location and block are unreported and Fig. 10(b) is not digitized, so location and aggregation cannot be matched to any Studio output.
The thermal-aware greedy task mapping and the TED+SCBO design-space optimization cannot be represented in a single fixed-power steady solve.
The paper links no code, configs or data, so inputs cannot be recovered or verified. There is also a minor 240 vs 256 GB/s NoC bandwidth inconsistency in the text.

Steady-state 2D conduction in the bundled Studio solver is used as an approximation of HotSpot 6.0 steady-state, with TIM, heat spreader and heat sink as lumped or layered package materials. Material properties are Studio defaults, since the paper only points to TESA [12] for values.
Ambient 45 C and convection resistance 0.4 K/W would be applied as the paper's stated boundary conditions only if a complete floorplan and power set were available.

No floorplan or power rows are provided in this extraction because block geometry and per-block watts are missing. Total chip power is not split among blocks without a published rule, and dimensions or powers from other scenarios (e.g., B1-B4, the 200 mm2 case) are not mixed in.
